sheet-69.description: The lower half of sheet 69, drawn at 100 feet to an inch below the title and key map, shows the Venetian lagoon development laid out on the salt marsh on the bay side of Sea Isle City, north-west of Central Avenue. Venicean Road runs along a narrow strip of filled land between the State Inland Waterway to the north and the Rio Delle Isole to the south, ending at its western end in a turning circle surrounded by wedge-shaped lots. At its eastern end it meets County Boulevard, which crosses the waterway on a wooden bridge and runs south-east towards the town between long rows of narrow numbered lots in blocks lettered A and B. Further east, Paris Place and the canals Rio Delle Barche and Rio Del Affare run parallel to the boulevard, each street a finger of land between two canals. Along the bottom edge the ends of Pearl Place, Neptune Place and Ariadne Place show between Rio Grand, Rio Delle Stelle, Rio Della Luna and Rio Delle Amore, with Dolphin Street and Porto Delle Salute at the lower left. Almost all of the lots are vacant: the only buildings are a few frame dwellings and boat houses at the junction of County Boulevard and Venicean Road and two boat houses on a small island in the waterway. A dashed water pipe follows County Boulevard and Venicean Road. The salt marsh between the beach and the waterway is lettered across the top of this part. The canals have since been filled, and the modern streets that follow these lots are numbered.
notes: County Boulevard is the line of modern 44th Street; Venicean Road keeps its name, but only its first stretch west of 44th Street survives.
Paris, Ariadne, Neptune and Pearl Places correspond to modern 43rd, 45th, 46th and 47th Places.

Placed from one hand-picked junction (County Boulevard / Venicean Road = 44th Street / Venicean Road) and a point derived from it along 44th Street at the atlas scale: low confidence, scale and rotation assumed.
The upper half of the sheet (title, key map of the town, water and fire department notes and legend) is not part of this annotation.

Printed sheet 69. Upper half: title, key map of the whole town (not to scale for georeferencing) and water/fire notes, left out. Lower half: to-scale map at 100 ft to an inch of the Venetian lagoon development north-west of Central Av: Venicean Road loop, County Boulevard (modern 44th Street), Paris Pl, Ariadne Pl, Neptune Pl, Pearl Pl (modern 43rd to 47th Place), Rio Delle Isole and other canals, State Inland Waterway. One part (the lower map); its only modern junction is 44th Street / Venicean Road.

sheet-70-1.description: Sheet 70, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that Landis Avenue runs up the page, covers the south end of Sea Isle City at Townsend's Inlet. The upper half is a regular grid: 11th to 14th Streets cross Roberts, Brewster, Landis Avenue and Railroad Avenue, with 15th Street at the right edge. These blocks are divided into narrow numbered lots and are almost all vacant; the U.S. Life Saving Station with its boat house stands between Landis and Railroad Avenues by 12th Street. A creek of the inlet's main channel cuts diagonally across the blocks west of Brewster, with a few small buildings along its bank. The lower half has a different, older layout of avenues running at an angle: Holly, Cedar, Rose, Storm, Surf and Whilden Avenues, crossed by Sounds Avenue along the channel and by a second Roberts and a second Landis Avenue. This is the built-up part of the inlet settlement, with dwellings, the Inlet House and beer garden, the Sea View Hotel, a club house, a pavilion and stores. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad enters from the lower left on a trestle across the channel from Leaming (Avalon), seven-eighths of a mile away, and curves north into Railroad Avenue. Townsend's Inlet is lettered along the left margin. An inset at the lower left, showing the yacht club and boat houses on the State Inland Waterway, is a separate annotation and not included here.
notes: 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th and 15th Streets are modern 77th, 78th, 79th, 80th and 81st Streets.
Brewster is modern Central Avenue; Railroad Avenue is modern Pleasure Avenue; Roberts in the upper grid is modern Roberts Avenue.

Holly, Cedar, Rose, Storm, Surf and Whilden Avenues and the lower Roberts and Landis Avenues follow a layout that has not survived; the modern streets there are 81st to 86th Streets at right angles to Landis Avenue. Control comes from the upper grid only, so the lower part of the sheet is extrapolated.
The modern Pleasure Avenue nodes at 77th and 78th Streets belong to a branch about 190 m east of the old Railroad Avenue and were excluded.

Printed sheet 70, 100 ft to an inch, turned: Landis Av runs up the page. South end of town (Townsends Inlet): 11th to 15th St (modern 77th to 81st Street), Roberts Av, Brewster (Central Avenue), Landis Av, Railroad Av (Pleasure Avenue); below them Holly, Cedar, Rose, Storm, Surf and Whilden Avs, Sounds Av and a second Roberts Av and Landis Av, a street layout with no modern counterpart. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower left (Sea Isle City Yacht Club and boat houses on the State Inland Waterway, marsh), no streets.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Sea Isle City Yacht Club and boat houses on the State Inland Waterway, marsh (no street junction and no feature drawn on another sheet).

sheet-71.description: Sheet 71, at 50 feet to an inch, covers four blocks of central Sea Isle City between Loretto Avenue on the left and Pearl on the right, from Central Avenue (or Brewster Street) at the top to Marine Place and the boardwalk at the bottom, with Shell and Dolphin crossing in between. Landis Avenue runs across the middle of the sheet and Railroad Avenue, carrying the single track of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), runs below it. The deep blocks between Central and Landis Avenues are mostly vacant lots, with only a few frame dwellings near Landis Avenue. Between Landis and Railroad Avenues there are scattered dwellings, a bake house with an oven and an auto house. The blocks between Railroad Avenue and the beach are more built up, with cottages and boarding houses facing the ocean: the Seminole, the Magnolia, bath houses and St. Mary's Home. Marine Place is drawn as a boardwalk with pavilions on the beach, and the Atlantic Ocean lies beyond. Each block is divided into numbered lots, with block numbers in heavy type and house numbers along the frontages; dashed lines mark the water pipes in the cross streets. A scale bar is printed in Railroad Avenue.
notes: Loretto, Shell, Dolphin and Pearl are modern 51st, 50th, 49th and 48th Streets.
Railroad Avenue, with the railroad in the street, is modern Pleasure Avenue; Central Avenue keeps its name.
Marine Place (the boardwalk) has no modern counterpart; the modern cross streets end at the promenade well inland of the 1909 beach front.

Printed sheet 71, 50 ft. Central Av (or Brewster St) to Marine Pl (boardwalk) between Loretto (51st Street) and Pearl (48th Street): Landis Av, Railroad Av (Pleasure Avenue, W.J.&S. R.R. in the street), Shell (50th), Dolphin (49th). One part.

sheet-72.description: Sheet 72, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the centre of Sea Isle City between Coral on the left and Minerva on the right, from Central Avenue (or Brewster Street) at the top to Marine Place and the boardwalk at the bottom, with Neptune and Ariadne crossing between. Landis Avenue, the main street, crosses the middle of the sheet, and Railroad Avenue below it carries the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad). The town's public buildings stand in the block between Central and Landis Avenues by Ariadne: the City Hall, drawn in brick, the public school, a livery and the Lincoln Hotel. The First M.E. Church faces Landis Avenue near Neptune, and a hardware store and tin shop stand by Ariadne. North of Landis Avenue the blocks hold frame dwellings and stores, among them the Colonade. South of Railroad Avenue are dwellings and cottages, with the Minerva House near Minerva. Marine Place runs along the beach as a boardwalk with pavilions, and the Atlantic Ocean lies beyond. Each block is divided into numbered lots, with block numbers in heavy type and house numbers along the frontages; dashed lines mark the water pipes in the cross streets.
notes: Coral, Neptune, Ariadne and Minerva are modern 47th, 46th, 45th and 44th Streets.
Railroad Avenue is modern Pleasure Avenue.
City Hall is the only brick building on the sheet.

Printed sheet 72, 50 ft. Central Av to Marine Pl between Pearl/Coral (47th Street) and Minerva (44th Street): Coral, Neptune (46th), Ariadne (45th); City Hall, public school, 1st M.E. Church. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-73-1.description: Sheet 73, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the business centre of Sea Isle City between Minerva on the left and Ocean Avenue on the right, from Central Avenue (or Brewster) at the top to Marine Place and the boardwalk at the bottom, with Paris, Italia and the narrow West Jersey Avenue crossing between. Ocean Avenue is drawn 165 feet wide, with the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad running down it to the station: the depot, freight house and platforms stand at the top right. Beside the tracks are the sheds, coal bins and office of the Sea Isle City Lumber Company. A branch track curves from Ocean Avenue across the blocks into Railroad Avenue, where the line continues south-west. Between Central and Landis Avenues are St. Joseph's Roman Catholic Church and its priest's house, a fire department hose wagon hall, a fire department hose cart and truck hall and the Girard Hotel. Along Landis Avenue are the post office, stores, boarding houses and the Lafayette House. South of Railroad Avenue the blocks hold cottages, bath houses, the Grand Central Hotel, a bowling alley and stores facing the boardwalk. An inset at the lower right showing the Casino on piles at the foot of Ocean Avenue is not part of this annotation. Each block is divided into numbered lots, with block numbers in heavy type and house numbers along the frontages; dashed lines mark the water pipes in the cross streets.
notes: Minerva, Paris and Italia are modern 44th, 43rd and 42nd Streets; West Jersey Avenue keeps its name.
Ocean Avenue is the line of modern John F. Kennedy Boulevard; its junctions were not detected and the boulevard is not used as control.
The Casino inset at the lower right was not placed (see the sheet's unplaced entry).

Printed sheet 73, 50 ft. Central Av to Marine Pl between Minerva (44th Street) and Ocean Av (John F. Kennedy Boulevard): Paris (43rd), Italia (42nd), West Jersey Av, W.J.&S. R.R. depot. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower right, the Casino built on piles at the foot of Ocean Av.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: the Casino on piles at the foot of Ocean Avenue, Marine Place boardwalk (no street junction; no feature reliably drawn on both the inset and sheet 74; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-74 at Ocean Avenue / Marine Place if a shared feature can be matched).

sheet-74.description: Sheet 74, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the blocks of Sea Isle City between Ocean Avenue on the left and Swain on the right, from Central Avenue (or Brewster) at the top to Marine Place and the boardwalk at the bottom, with Fritz and Garrison crossing between. Ocean Avenue, 165 feet wide, carries the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, and two lines curve away from it: the West Jersey and Seashore line running north-east between Central and Landis Avenues, and the Atlantic City Railroad (Philadelphia and Reading) along the top of the sheet, with its depot, freight house and coal bins. The Sea Isle City Water Company pumping station and stand pipe stand by Central Avenue. Along Landis Avenue are the Depot Hotel, Hotel Bellevue, Petersen's Hotel with its beer garden, the Tivoli Hotel, the Philadelphia House, Busch's Hotel and the Central House, with printing and drug stores. The M. Wells Ice Company and the lumber yard and sheds of C. H. Clouting Company occupy the block by Garrison. Near the beach are the Sea Isle City Electric Light Company engine and dynamo room, the Excursion House with bath houses, the Pennsylvania House, the Surf House and a carousel, with approaches to the boardwalk. Each block is divided into numbered lots, with block numbers in heavy type and house numbers along the frontages; dashed lines mark the water pipes in the cross streets.
notes: Fritz, Garrison and Swain are modern 40th, 39th and 38th Streets; Ocean Avenue is the line of John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
The Atlantic City Railroad and the West Jersey and Seashore line north of Ocean Avenue are gone.

Printed sheet 74, 50 ft. Central Av to Marine Pl between Ocean Av (John F. Kennedy Boulevard) and Swain (38th Street): Fritz (40th), Garrison (39th); Atlantic City R.R. depot, water works, hotels, electric light plant. One part.

sheet-75-1.description: The upper strip of sheet 75, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the blocks of Sea Isle City between Spring on the left and Ludlam on the right, from Landis Avenue at the top to Marine Place and the boardwalk at the bottom, with Union and Prince crossing between. Railroad Avenue, carrying the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), runs across the middle of the strip. This is a thinly built part of the town at its south-western edge: the blocks are divided into numbered lots, most of them vacant. A few frame dwellings and auto houses stand in the blocks between Railroad Avenue and the beach near Spring, and at the right edge, by Ludlam, the All Saints Sea Shore Home faces the boardwalk. Marine Place is drawn as a boardwalk along the beach, with the Atlantic Ocean beyond. A heavy line at the bottom separates this strip from the lower one, which shows another group of blocks further north-east. Water pipes are drawn in Landis Avenue and the cross streets.
notes: Spring, Union, Prince and Ludlam are modern 58th, 57th, 56th and 55th Streets; Railroad Avenue is modern Pleasure Avenue.

Printed sheet 75, 50 ft. Two strips divided by a heavy line, both Landis Av to Marine Pl: part 1 (upper) Spring (58th Street) to Ludlam (55th Street) with Union (57th), Prince (56th); part 2 (lower) Hammonton (54th) to Loretto (51st) with Vineland (53rd), Albion (52nd).

sheet-75-2.description: The lower strip of sheet 75, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the blocks of Sea Isle City between Hammonton on the left and Loretto Avenue on the right, from Landis Avenue at the top to Marine Place and the boardwalk at the bottom, with Vineland and Albion crossing between. Railroad Avenue, carrying the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), runs across the middle of the strip, and a scale bar is printed in it. The blocks north of Railroad Avenue are entirely vacant apart from two dwellings by Vineland. Between Railroad Avenue and the beach are a few dwellings and larger cottages: Gordon's Sea View, The Mansion, and St. Joseph's Convent by Loretto Avenue. Marine Place runs along the beach as a boardwalk, with the Atlantic Ocean beyond. A heavy line at the top separates this strip from the upper one, which shows blocks further south-west. Each block carries its block number and numbered lots, with house numbers along Marine Place and water pipes in the cross streets.
notes: Hammonton, Vineland, Albion and Loretto are modern 54th, 53rd, 52nd and 51st Streets; Railroad Avenue is modern Pleasure Avenue.

Printed sheet 75, 50 ft. Two strips divided by a heavy line, both Landis Av to Marine Pl: part 1 (upper) Spring (58th Street) to Ludlam (55th Street) with Union (57th), Prince (56th); part 2 (lower) Hammonton (54th) to Loretto (51st) with Vineland (53rd), Albion (52nd).

sheet-76-1.description: The left strip of sheet 76, at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that Landis Avenue runs up the page, covers the northern end of Sea Isle City from Rosewood at the bottom to Hancock Avenue at the top, between Sea Isle Avenue on the bay side and the ocean beach. Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, Girard and Prospect Avenues, Devon, Landsdowne and Belmont cross between. Sea Isle Avenue carries the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad and the Philadelphia and Reading line side by side; Landis Avenue and Railroad Avenue run parallel to it, and Marine Place follows the beach as a boardwalk. The blocks are divided into numbered lots and are nearly all vacant. The only large buildings are the Catholic Home between Hancock and Pennsylvania Avenues and the Continental Hotel, with its bath houses and platform, between Girard and Prospect Avenues, both near the beach, with a few dwellings along the ocean front. A strip of blocks west of Sea Isle Avenue is cut by the left edge. A heavy line at the right separates this strip from the second strip of the sheet, which shows the blocks further south-west.
notes: Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, Girard, Prospect, Devon, Landsdowne, Belmont and Rosewood are modern 22nd to 29th Streets; Hancock Avenue has no modern counterpart.

Sea Isle Avenue, Railroad Avenue and Marine Place have no modern counterpart here; control is the eight junctions along Landis Avenue only, so the part is a helmert fit (position, scale and rotation).

Printed sheet 76, 100 ft to an inch, turned (Landis Av runs up the page). North end of town, Sea Isle Av (with the railroads) to Marine Pl and the ocean. Two strips divided by a heavy line: part 1 (left) Rosewood (29th Street) to Hancock (north of 22nd Street) with Belmont, Lansdowne, Devon, Prospect, Girard, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; part 2 (right) Swain (38th Street) to Westphalia (30th Street) with Hartson, House, Mathilda, Maxham, Farrand, Elm, Atlantic.

sheet-76-2.description: The right strip of sheet 76, at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that Landis Avenue runs up the page, covers the north-eastern blocks of Sea Isle City from Swain at the bottom to Westphalia at the top, between Sea Isle Avenue on the bay side and the ocean beach. Hartson, House, Mathilda, Maxham, Farrand, Elm and Atlantic cross between. Sea Isle Avenue, 100 to 150 feet wide, carries the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad and the Philadelphia and Reading line; Landis Avenue and Railroad Avenue run parallel to it, and Marine Place follows the beach as a boardwalk. The blocks near Swain are the most built up, with dwellings, boarding houses, The Aldine, the Sea View House and the lumber yard of C. H. Clouting Company with its carpenter shop beside the railroad. Further north-east the blocks thin out to scattered cottages along the beach, and United States Life Saving Station buildings between Elm and Farrand and by Westphalia. The strip adjoins sheet 74 at Swain. A heavy line at the left separates it from the other strip of the sheet.
notes: Westphalia, Atlantic, Elm, Farrand, Maxham, Mathilda, House, Hartson and Swain are modern 30th to 38th Streets; Railroad Avenue is modern Pleasure Avenue.
The drawn blocks bend slightly near Westphalia, and the fit leaves residuals of 2 to 5 m at the north end.

Printed sheet 76, 100 ft to an inch, turned (Landis Av runs up the page). North end of town, Sea Isle Av (with the railroads) to Marine Pl and the ocean. Two strips divided by a heavy line: part 1 (left) Rosewood (29th Street) to Hancock (north of 22nd Street) with Belmont, Lansdowne, Devon, Prospect, Girard, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; part 2 (right) Swain (38th Street) to Westphalia (30th Street) with Hartson, House, Mathilda, Maxham, Farrand, Elm, Atlantic.
